inicio.kicker: AI Management Program 2027 · G5 · closing · 8 lessons
inicio.lead: An agent that works today isn't enough: someone has to answer for it, see what it did, know whether it's good, and improve it without losing control. In eight lessons you name the people accountable, check permissions and the log, set up evaluation and indicators, run a LOOP-R cycle with a return loop, and close the program with the final project in Gestoria.
inicio.capa_alt: The sales manager and the owner of a distributor look together at a panel of five indicators on the wall; in the background, through the glass, the stock of jugs of cleaning products.

numeros.t: final project with the program rubric

inicio.aulas_sub: In the order in which operations gain governance: who answers, what is allowed and logged, how you evaluate and measure, how you improve with a return loop, what the law requires. Lesson 8 brings it all together in the program's final project.

cursos.sub: This is G5, the closing. The final project in lesson 8 uses everyone's deliverables: process (G2), agents (G3), resources (G4), people (G1), and governance and measurement (G5). Courses not yet published open as they become ready.

itens.t: The agentic company and the 2027 manager
itens.l: What changed in management, what the consultancies say, Brazil, the career, and your first process.
Take the process apart before automating it: eliminate, simplify, redesign, and decide who does each step.
Job role, delegation, constitution, authority limit, progressive trust, agent team, and exception queue.
Choose a model for each case, take care of context and company knowledge, and measure cost per outcome.
What stays with people, the conversation about change, the junior who supervises agents, and team training.
Accountable people, permissions, and log; evaluation and indicators; a LOOP-R cycle with a rollback and the final project in Gestoria.

itens: Area managers, owners of small or mid-sized companies, and operations or HR leaders who already have AI agents working on the team.
For people who don't code and don't want to: here you govern, measure, and improve the operation. Building an agent is a different course.

For people who took the other courses in the program (or have their pieces) and want to wrap up with the final project. You can do it on your own, but lesson 8 pays off more with your deliverables from G2, G3, and G4.

blocos.t: What you'll be able to do
itens: A responsibility matrix where whoever enters it does not approve it, and every agent has a person who is accountable for it.
An identity, permission, and log checklist applied to your agent, with a monthly review scheduled.
A set of 30 cases with an answer key and a dashboard of 5 indicators with a denominator and a baseline.
A logged LOOP-R cycle, with hypothesis, test, decision, and the rollback trigger written down before you promote.

blocos.t: The case that runs through the course
itens: Horizonte Distribuidora, a 40-person fictional study company that distributes cleaning products in the interior of São Paulo.

You play Patrícia Lima, sales manager, who is responsible for Hora, the agent that sells over WhatsApp. Carlos, the owner, wants to extend Hora to collections; you ask that the decision wait until the operation is governed and measured.
The lab's failures become management problems: an agent with IT as the accountable person, the log turned off, a tool switched on with a "go ahead" on WhatsApp, and a dashboard without a baseline.
